html:
Mahavira, born Vardhamana, was a teacher of the Ganges plain whom Jains honour as the 24th and last Tirthankara, a "ford-maker" who shows the way across the cycle of rebirth. Jain tradition dates him to 599 to 527 BCE; many scholars place him somewhat later, as an older contemporary of the Buddha.

He was born a prince near Vaishali, in today's Bihar. At about thirty he left home and lived as a wandering ascetic for over twelve years, then reached kevala, full knowledge, and taught for some thirty years in Magadha and nearby lands.

His teaching, the core of Jainism:

  • Ahimsa, not harming any living being, down to insects and plants.
  • Truth, not stealing, chastity and non-attachment to possessions.
  • Every living thing has a soul bound by karma, which strict self-discipline can free.

He built on the teachings of earlier Tirthankaras such as Parshvanatha. Jainism, like Buddhism, grew among merchants of the Mahajanapadas, and the Maurya founder Chandragupta is said to have become a Jain monk. Mahatma Gandhi drew on Jain ideas of non-violence.
